_comment: A niche is defined by tags, because tags are what Steam actually sorts on
and what a buyer browses by. Tag names are Steam's own and are fussy:
'RTS' is real, 'Real Time Strategy' is not, and asking SteamSpy for a tag
that does not exist gets you a silent junk list rather than an error.
Greenlight refuses those rather than analysing them - if a tag name is
wrong you will be told, not quietly given numbers about Grand Theft Auto.
require_tags : a game must carry ALL of these. Keep it to one or two.
any_tags     : and at least one of these. This is the theme filter, and it
is the easiest thing to get wrong - see the note below.
keywords     : optional, matched against name and tags.
sample_cap   : how many of the biggest games to fetch details for. Each
one costs about three seconds on a cold cache.
sample_released_since : named for its scope. Release dates only exist after
the per-game pass, so this filters the detail sample and NOT
the population the revenue figures come from.
ALWAYS read the random slice in the report before trusting a number. It is
there to catch exactly the mistake made below.

_note: 'Modern' was in any_tags and had to come out. It means modern SETTING,
not modern military, so it admitted any contemporary RTS - Laptop
Tycoon sat near the median of a supposedly military niche. The tag
filter was doing exactly what it was told; what it was told was wrong.
drone-rts.name: Modern-military RTS (the Drone Command niche)
